INDIANAPOLIS, Nov. 2, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Allison Transmission Holdings Inc. (NYSE: ALSN), today reported third quarter net sales of $1,534 million with an adjusted EBITDA margin of 26.1 percent and net cash provided by operating activities of $343 million and raised full year 2026 guidance.
Third quarter results include segment reporting for Allison Transmission, the Company's legacy business, excluding certain costs now accounted for within the Allison Central Group, and Allison Off-Highway, the business acquired from Dana Incorporated on January 1, 2026. The Allison Central Group is a centralized cost center which includes certain functional costs that support the Company's global operations.
The most directly comparable GAAP measure to adjusted EBITDA and adjusted EBITDA margin is net income or segment operating profit (loss) in the case of our segments and net income as a percent of net sales ("net income margin") or segment operating profit (loss) as a percent of net sales in the case of our segments, respectively. Adjusted EBITDA is calculated as earnings before interest expense, net, income tax expense, amortization of intangible assets, depreciation of property, plant and equipment and other adjustments as defined by the Second Amended and Restated Credit Agreement dated as of March 29, 2019, as amended, governing Allison Transmission, Inc.'s term loans and revolving credit facility.

## Quarterly Performance Highlights
The company reported adjusted EBITDA of $400 million, up 56% from $256 million in the prior-year period, with an adjusted EBITDA margin of 26.1%. Net income reached $191 million, or 12.5% of net sales, compared to $137 million in Q3 2025.
## Segment Performance Analysis
Allison Transmission, the legacy business, delivered record quarterly net sales of $881 million, up 27% year-over-year, with a robust gross margin of 46.2% and adjusted EBITDA margin of 37.8%. Operating income reached $300 million, representing 34.1% of segment sales.
Allison Off-Highway, acquired on January 1, 2026, contributed $653 million in net sales with a gross margin of 15.0% and adjusted EBITDA margin of 12.7%. Operating income was $32 million, or 4.9% of segment sales. Management noted that off-highway margins are typically weaker in the third quarter due to European holiday shutdowns and seasonal factors.
The Central Group Function, representing corporate overhead, recorded an operating loss of $28 million, resulting in consolidated operating income of $304 million, or 19.8% of total net sales.
Net income guidance for 2026 was set at $645 million to $685 million, with management noting the outlook includes one-time expenses tied to separation, integration, and restructuring of the off-highway business, as well as inventory step-up costs and acquisition-related cash outlays. Capital expenditure expectations were reduced to $240 million to $260 million from $260 million to $280 million.

ceramic.snippet: Intense Competition and Evolving Consumer Preferences: Gap Inc. operates in a highly competitive and dynamic apparel retail market. The company faces significant pressure from fast-fashion retailers, online-only brands, and other established apparel companies, which constantly vie for market share. Rapidly changing fashion trends, increasing consumer demand for sustainable and ethically produced clothing, and the accelerated shift towards online shopping necessitate continuous adaptation. The inability to consistently meet evolving consumer demands and adapt to fast fashion cycles can lead to \"fashion misses\" and sales declines, as seen with some brands like Athleta. Consumers also face low switching costs, intensifying price-driven purchasing.   Macroeconomic Headwinds and Tariff Impacts: Gap Inc. is susceptible to broader global economic conditions, including inflationary pressures, geopolitical instability, and fluctuations in consumer spending. A significant and frequently cited risk is the direct financial impact of tariffs, which have reduced gross margins and are expected to continue to do so. Management estimated tariffs would reduce consolidated operating margin by approximately 100-110 basis points in fiscal 2025, and projected a Q1 2026 gross margin shrink of 150-200 basis points due to these impacts.   Supply Chain Disruptions and Operational Inefficiency: The company faces ongoing challenges in its global supply chain, which can be affected by geopolitical tensions, natural disasters, transportation shortages, factory closures, and inventory mismanagement. These disruptions can impact product availability, delivery, and ultimately, sales. Furthermore, Gap's \"design-to-shelf\" cycle is slower compared to fast-fashion rivals, undermining its ability to quickly respond to trend shifts and maintain inventory efficiency.

## Allison Transmission Revenue Climbs 121% Y/Y to $1.53 Billion Amidst Strategic Acquisition

## Summary

Allison Transmission reported a 121% Y/Y increase in consolidated net sales to $1.53 billion, fueled by the $2.6 billion acquisition of its new Off-Highway segment. This unit contributed $653 million in quarterly revenue. While the core Allison Transmission business sustained growth, reporting 27% Y/Y net sales expansion, the consolidated gross profit margin contracted to 33% from 48% in the prior-year period. This dilution reflects the different manufacturing and overhead profile of the acquired assets.

The transformation into a dual-segment entity introduces execution risks. Combined operating income for the quarter reached $304 million, representing a 20% margin, down from 29% a year ago. Integration efforts are underway, with the company recording $17 million in restructuring charges in Q3 and $30 million in acquisition-related expenses YTD.

The balance sheet reflects the capital required for this expansion. Long-term debt climbed to $3.99 billion from $2.89 billion at year-end 2025. Despite this leverage, operating cash flow remains resilient, totaling $811 million YTD, an increase from $593 million during the same period in 2025.

Footnote analysis indicates significant structural changes. Post-acquisition goodwill sits at $2.83 billion, with $638 million specifically allocated to the Off-Highway segment. Additionally, the company recognized $31 million in deferred revenue liabilities and acquired $88 million in total lease obligations. The path forward depends on the integration of these off-highway assets and the ability to expand their operating margins beyond the 5% rate reported this quarter.
